title: 12 PROJECTS THAT SHOW WHAT EDT ACTUALLY BUILDS
dek: No pitch-deck language, just the work — twelve activations, installations and realtime characters we've shipped across Malaysia and the region, with the numbers each one actually posted.
intro: Every one of these started as a brief that sounded slightly too ambitious — a hologram that had to hold a real conversation, a projection that had to win against a live jury, an AI persona that had to talk back on a golf course. We build the technical layer other studios say is too complex, then we ship it.

entries.blurb: MCMC's induction used to be a slide deck and a printed handbook — forgettable by the second slide. We rebuilt it as a VR game new hires actually finish, learning the organisation by moving through it instead of sitting through it. It's the reason MetaHRise now holds a Malaysia Book of Records entry, not the other way around.

Mascots are usually a photo op — wave, pose, move on. The brief asked for one that could actually talk, so we gave Tiger a realtime voice and a face that performs in sync with it. What's in the recap isn't a demo-reel moment; it's an unscripted exchange, captured live on the course.

Think City wanted heritage buildings to speak for themselves without another plaque nobody reads. We layered the stories into AR instead — point a phone at a building and the history behind it surfaces on the spot. It's since travelled further than the brief asked for: the same trail has been picked up in twelve countries.

A festival footprint only means something if people actually walk it. ARFestKL needed Downtown KL turned into a trail dense enough to survive a full weekend of foot traffic, so we built a QR-to-AR funnel engineered to take the volume without breaking. It held — over fifty thousand impressions and twelve thousand scans in two days.

Ikat weaving is generations of technique that doesn't survive well behind glass. The Ministry of Textile wanted people to feel the craft, not just read a wall label about it, so we staged the history as a full immersive environment instead of a static display. It pulled RM3.2 million in media value and over 5,800 visitors through the doors.

A founders' story told as wall text gets skimmed once and forgotten. AirAsia wanted theirs to be a place people actually walk through, so we combined interactive walls, AR overlays and an AI layer into one permanent gallery — the story you touch, not just read.
entries.statLine: Interactive walls + AR + AI, permanent install

entries.blurb: Sneaker drops live and die on how they photograph. For Grey Day, New Balance needed an experience people would actually queue for and post, so we put a realtime AR try-on inside a fully immersive room built to look good from every angle a phone camera finds.
entries.imageAlt: New Balance Grey Day AR try-on room

entries.blurb: A counter needs staffing; a hologram doesn't. Malaysia Airlines needed a first point of contact at MATIC KL that could answer real questions, so we deployed an AI stewardess as a hologram — live, responsive, and on duty for every visitor who walks up.

A tower this size needed a lobby that didn't feel like an afterthought. PNB wanted the building's own story told at its base, so we built the largest interactive wall EDT has shipped for a single structure — the tower's history, made touchable by anyone walking in.
entries.statLine: Largest interactive install built for the tower

entries.blurb: Supersale needed broadcast-grade sets on a campaign timeline, not a construction schedule. We ran the whole shoot through ARVENA, EDT's virtual production platform, building every set in-engine instead of on a soundstage — same polish, none of the build time.

Safi didn't want a spokesperson who ages out of a campaign — they wanted a persona that's entirely theirs. We built Shayla from scratch: a face, a voice, and a posting schedule, deployed as a fully virtual influencer for the national campaign.

You can't schedule an earthquake to train for it. Tokyo Fire Department needed responders to feel the disorientation before the real event does, so we built a VR simulation that puts them through the shake — training that rehearses a moment training usually can't reach.
entries.imageAlt: Tokyo Fire Department VR earthquake simulation

cta.heading: Got a brief that sounds too ambitious?
cta.body: That's usually the one we want. Tell us what you're trying to build and we'll tell you exactly how EDT would ship it.
